thread:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Cobalt Health (tenant:cobalt) - elevated 5xx rates on VPC dedicated pool canary (region us-west-2). Alerting threshold breached: 5xx > 4% sustained for 5m. Automated canary gate flagged.
jen-sre: I'm on it. what's the scope?
matt-oncall: seeing ~6% 5xx for canary traffic slice (~3% of their traffic). Latency also spiked from 120ms -> 450ms for some requests.
lina-infra: logs show a spike of OOM logs on the canary instances shortly before errors. stack traces look like KV cache eviction thrash.
jen-sre: tagging @cobalt-engops and @sam-cs for visibility. Sam, are they on-call on their side?
sam-cs: Cobalt ops are looped in, they confirmed they're watching. They said customer-visible impact is small but rising — their UI queued some inference calls.
cobalt-engops: Confirmed, we see retries from our side. Customer wants minimal disruption. Prefer rolling back the canary artifact to the previous pinned version if safe.
alex-eng: Quick note on artifacts: canary was pinned to model-serving v2.4.0-canary. Previous pinned for cobalt was v2.3.0.
jen-sre: Ok plan outline: 1) Quarantine canary traffic to dedicated canary pool (already in place) 2) Pin back to v2.3.0 for cobalt tenant only 3) Gradually divert canary slice to pinned artifact and monitor 4) If healthy, promote. If not, isolate further and route to reserved fallback.
matt-oncall: I'll take lead on the pinback operation. handing off from @jen-sre (current oncall).
jen-sre: Handoff notes: console traces for the canary show these recent errors:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:07Z cobalt-canary-1 kubelet: container killed: OOMKilled
2026-03-15T03:12:09Z model-server: kv-cache: eviction > 80% -> cache thrash
2026-03-15T03:12:12Z model-server: grpc:error: upstream error: "runtime/panic"
```
jen-sre: Suggest pinback because this looks triggered by a memory regression introduced in 2.4.0-canary under specific request patterns.
matt-oncall: Performing pinback now. Command: `rbctl artifacts pin --tenant cobalt --artifact v2.3.0 --scope tenant`
alex-eng: Note: this will update routing in the VPC control plane for cobalt only. Canary pool will still exist but will route requests to the pinned artifact.
matt-oncall: Running...
```
$ rbctl artifacts pin --tenant cobalt --artifact v2.3.0 --scope tenant
Started job: job-873241
Job status: applying pin to routing mesh for tenant cobalt
```
matt-oncall: job-873241 reports success after ~45s.
lina-infra: I see new pods coming up on v2.3.0 for cobalt in canary pool, healthchecks passing.
matt-oncall: Diverting 100% of canary slice traffic to pinned artifact for observation. Command: `rbctl traffic shift --tenant cobalt --slice canary --pct 100`
jen-sre: Keep an eye on 5xx and p99 latency. Set short monitoring window: 1m evaluation with 75% pass requirement.
alex-eng: Metrics starting to trend down: 5xx for cobalt dropped from 6% -> 0.9% within 2 mins. p99 latency back to ~130ms.
sam-cs: Customer update: Cobalt ops say core flows are passing, some UI queues cleared. They're cautiously optimistic.
cobalt-engops: We still see a small number of older in-flight requests failing; new requests are fine. Thanks for the fast turn.
jen-sre: Good. Next steps: keep pinned until we complete a canary root-cause. We'll schedule a controlled repro against v2.4.0-canary in staging. Also create a follow-up ticket for post-incident analysis and memory profiling.
matt-oncall: Creating incident follow-up: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0342 (assigned to eng-runtime).
lina-infra: I'm collecting heap dumps and thread profiles from affected pods; saving artifacts to /artifacts/cobalt/3419876543.
jen-sre: Customer-facing wording (sam, feel free to copy/edit): "We've identified a memory regression in a canary release that affected a small fraction of your traffic. We've pinned your tenant to the previous validated release (v2.3.0) and traffic has returned to normal. We're investigating and will share a timeline for full remediation."
sam-cs: Sending update now. cc @cobalt-engops :thumbsup:
cobalt-engops: Appreciate the fast action. We'll hold on promotions until we get root-cause and mem-profiles.
jen-sre: On-call handoff: matt remains primary until 09:30 UTC. I'll remain secondarily available. If any regression reappears, escalate to eng-runtime and pages.
matt-oncall: Acknowledged. Setting slack reminder to re-evaluate at +30m.
inc-bot: Reminder set: Re-evaluate canary health for cobalt in 30m (job-873241).
alex-eng: Quick ask: we should also add a canary-automation guard to fail fast on cache-memory growth > 70% for canary artifacts. Filing a small task.
jen-sre: Agreed. Add to the incident ticket.
sam-cs: Closing loop with customer: Cobalt accepted the update and will hold off on any client-side retries for 15m while we stabilize.
matt-oncall: Monitoring window complete; metrics remain stable. I'll leave the pin in place and schedule a controlled repro with eng-runtime for 16:00 UTC.
jen-sre: Thanks everyone. After repro and fix we can plan a careful re-roll with canary observability toggles. Postmortem to include: sequence of events, memory regression root cause, improved canary guard thresholds, and customer communication timeline. :white_check_mark:
